verdicts.evidence: 10-seed experiments on the paper's Linear DGP (K=3, n_k=2000, alpha=0.1) show MDCP worst-case coverage of 0.905 (classification) and 0.909 (regression), both above the 0.90 nominal target, with the parametric-fit deviation being appropriate for a linear DGP and shared across all methods.

500 seeded finite-measure LP instances (3 sources, 24 outcomes, alpha=0.1) solved with scipy.optimize.linprog show max primal-dual gap 2.23e-8, max complementary-slackness error 2.23e-8, max superlevel-structure violation 1.26e-8, and all 500 instances have at least one active source, directly confirming the dual optimality, KKT structure, and complementary slackness.

8 sample sizes (100–25,000 per source) × 20 seeds on 64-outcome categorical distributions show sup shared-score error dropping from 3.92 to 0.392 (Spearman −1.000) and calibrated-set symmetric difference from 18.45 to 1.80 (within oracle boundary of 3); a frozen-dual-weight destructive control yields 2.34× worse error, isolating the theorem's consistency assumption.

Measured reduction is 4.73% (SE 1.68) vs claimed 34.39%; even a cheating oracle constant-lambda search achieves only 13.49%. A known deviation (full-batch Adam instead of minibatch with early stopping) plausibly explains the gap, and the official 100-trial panel has not completed, so the shortfall cannot be attributed to the method being wrong nor the claim confirmed.

Measured reduction is 8.71% (SE 1.85) vs claimed 22.44%; oracle constant-lambda achieves 11.91%. Same optimizer deviation as Claim 4 applies, and the official 100-trial panel is incomplete, leaving the efficiency magnitude undetermined.
No FMoW images, DenseNet-121 checkpoint, or six-region prediction artifacts were used; no experiments were run for this claim.

overall: The logbook provides strong computational evidence for the three theorem claims: finite-sample coverage validity (empirical worst-case coverage above nominal), Theorem 2 dual optimality (500 LP instances with KKT checks passing to numerical precision), and Theorem 3 asymptotic convergence (clear convergence trends with a destructive control isolating the key assumption). The two empirical efficiency claims (classification 34.39%, regression 22.44%) remain inconclusive due to a known optimizer deviation and incomplete official-code runs, and the FMoW claim was not attempted at all.
